name: Liberalism in the United States
summary: The American liberal tradition rests on the founding's Lockean principles: equal natural rights, government by consent, constitutional limits, free speech and religion, and separation of church and state. From the Progressive Era and especially Franklin Roosevelt's New Deal, it added an active federal government that regulates business, supports organized labor, taxes progressively and provides social insurance, on the view that freedom also needs economic security. At its mid-century peak it joined this mixed economy with civil rights, Keynesian economic management, free trade and an anticommunist internationalism built around the UN and the Western alliance.
scope: The mainstream American liberal tradition as a whole, anchored on its mid-twentieth-century peak: the New Deal, Truman's Fair Deal and the Cold War liberalism of Truman, Kennedy, Humphrey and Americans for Democratic Action through the Great Society, read against the founding Lockean liberalism of the Declaration and the Bill of Rights from which it claims descent. It differs from modern-liberalism-in-the-united-states, which represents the contemporary Democratic program (2024 platform, Rawlsian egalitarianism) with its stances on abortion, LGBT and transgender rights, climate, and a more skeptical view of military power: this profile answers those later questions only as low-confidence inferences, and it is more hawkish and anticommunist, more pro-growth and pro-trade, and closer to the classical strand on property and markets. Where the founding classical strand and the New Deal strand split (markets, property, economic freedom) the answer is 0. It excludes libertarianism, American conservatism, the New Left and democratic socialism.

sources.usedFor: Contrast of classical and new liberalism on property, markets and redistribution; positive liberty; American welfare-state liberalism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Truman asked Congress for prepaid national health insurance so every American could afford care, though the program never passed and later liberals worked through mixed public and private coverage.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Truman's 1949 message asked to lift the federal minimum to at least 75 cents an hour, continuing the New Deal's wage floor.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The founding Jeffersonian strand trusted free markets while New Deal liberals saw markets as needing government management, so the tradition's strands are split on this comparison.

public-ownership.rationale: Roosevelt opposed state ownership of the means of production, with public power projects such as the TVA as the main exception.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: New Deal liberals favored progressive taxation, and Truman proposed new revenue mainly from corporations plus higher rates on upper-bracket incomes.

unions-good.rationale: The New Deal's Wagner Act guaranteed collective bargaining and Truman demanded repeal of Taft-Hartley as unfair to workers; strong support for organized labor is a hallmark of the tradition.

property-fundamental.rationale: Lockean founding liberalism treated property as a natural right, but New Deal liberals accepted regulating and limiting it for social ends, so the strands pull in opposite directions.

regulate-corporations.rationale: From Progressive-era trust regulation to New Deal securities and banking laws, liberals saw concentrated corporate power as a threat to be regulated.

cut-welfare.rationale: Social Security and unemployment insurance are the tradition's signature achievements, and Truman sought to widen coverage and raise benefits rather than cut them.

worker-ownership.rationale: Liberals defended free enterprise working alongside government and unions rather than collective worker ownership of firms.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Cold War liberals sometimes accepted curbs on liberty against subversion while also opposing McCarthyism, so the tradition pulls both ways on security surveillance.

strong-leader.rationale: Liberals favored vigorous presidential leadership, as Kennedy called for a government that uses its full powers, but within constitutional checks rather than bypassing them.

state-harmful.rationale: Kennedy said that where government has a job to do it should do it, and Truman described free government and free enterprise working together; the state is seen as an instrument of the general welfare.

limit-guns.rationale: The founding liberal ideals included the right to bear arms while later liberals favored gun regulation, so the tradition is divided on strict limits.

empower-police-military.rationale: Cold War liberals backed high military spending and strong defense, but the tradition is wary of police power over civil liberties, so it is mixed overall.

decide-locally.rationale: New Deal liberalism expanded federal power over the states, though Kennedy denied that liberals oppose local government.

traditional-family.rationale: Mid-century liberals did not challenge the traditional family, while later liberals backed women's equality and new family forms, so the strands differ.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The issue postdates the tradition's peak; later heirs of the tradition backed same-sex marriage as an extension of equal rights.

abortion-legal.rationale: Reproductive rights became part of the liberal program only after the 1960s, so this is an inference from the tradition's later development.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: After 1945 northern liberals made civil rights central, from Truman's civil rights program to the Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts, though southern Democrats resisted.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: American liberals celebrated the nation's founding traditions while welcoming change and new ideas, so the tradition is ambivalent here.

gradual-change.rationale: American liberalism worked through elections, legislation and the courts to reform institutions step by step, and moderates distanced themselves from radical progressives.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Following Wilson, Roosevelt and Truman built the United Nations and a world organization for peace, though with a US veto.

free-trade.rationale: Roosevelt sought to expand foreign trade and Truman asked Congress to restore the Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act; later liberals were more skeptical of trade deals such as NAFTA.

nation-first.rationale: Liberal internationalism held that US security depends on world cooperation through the UN and recovery programs rather than going it alone.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Cold War liberals backed containment and foreign commitments, though hawks and doves divided sharply over Vietnam.

open-borders.rationale: The tradition accepted national immigration control while seeking fairer admission; nothing in it supports open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Truman championed abundant production, resource development and growth that benefits everyone, the opposite of limiting growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy postdates the tradition's peak; later liberals backed the Paris Agreement.

revolution-justified.rationale: The Declaration of Independence asserts the people's right to alter or abolish a government that destroys their rights, a founding text of the tradition.

experts-over-public.rationale: New Deal liberalism relied on expert administration but remained committed to democratic consent, so it does not rank experts above the public.

central-planning.rationale: Liberals rejected state socialism and saw free enterprise as the main source of prosperity, with government steering rather than planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: The tradition defended private enterprise and rejected worker or state ownership as the basis of the economy.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Truman asked Congress to revise estate and gift taxes as part of raising revenue from those best able to pay.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Liberals from Roosevelt to Truman cut tariffs through reciprocal trade agreements rather than relying on protection.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Truman proposed federal river-basin development, public power and government loans or construction where private steel capacity fell short.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Jeffersonian and Jacksonian liberals prized small proprietors and Truman wanted water for family farms, but New Deal liberals accepted large corporations balanced by labor and regulation.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The tradition defends a market economy with wages and free enterprise.

one-party-rule.rationale: Kennedy grounded liberalism in faith in the people's reason and judgment, and the founding rests government on consent, both incompatible with single-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The tradition began in revolt against a king and established a republic without monarchy or hereditary aristocracy.

democracy-best.rationale: Democracy and consent of the governed are the common foundation of American liberalism, and Kennedy professed faith in citizens' reason and judgment.

direct-votes.rationale: Progressive-era liberals pushed initiatives and referendums, while the founding design relied on representatives, so the strands differ.

workers-councils.rationale: American liberals worked through elected legislatures and rejected socialist forms of rule.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Declaration holds that all men are created equal, rejecting a natural ruling class.

political-violence-never.rationale: The tradition honors the revolution against Britain yet rejects violence inside a working democracy, so it does not hold that violence is never justified.

separate-church-state.rationale: Separation of church and state is listed among the shared foundations of American liberalism.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The tradition grounds law in consent and reason with church and state kept apart.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Declaration treats justice and defense as duties of government, and Truman upheld public armed forces.

military-superiority.rationale: Cold War liberals backed high military spending and maintaining armed forces to deter aggression.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The tradition defines the nation by shared ideals and opposed admission policies based on ethnic discrimination.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Truman described employers and workers sharing prosperity under free enterprise rather than locked in class war.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Liberals sought fair opportunity and economic security, not equality of outcome.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Classical liberal economics valued self-interest in markets, but New Deal and Kennedy liberals stressed concern for others' welfare, so the strands differ.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The tradition begins from unalienable individual rights that government exists to secure.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Mid-century liberals talked about conservation as wise use of resources, not nature's intrinsic value; later environmentalism differs.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Liberals celebrated industrial expansion, rising production and the material gains of the postwar economy.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The issue postdates the tradition's peak and liberals balance civil liberty against security, so no clear answer.

restore-past-order.rationale: Kennedy defined a liberal as someone who looks ahead rather than behind and welcomes new ideas.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Kennedy said liberalism is an attitude of mind rather than a fixed creed, in keeping with the pragmatic, experimental spirit of the New Deal.

direct-action.rationale: The tradition pursued change through elections, Congress and the courts.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The tradition celebrates material progress and abundance.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Liberals accept a modern industrial economy and specialization.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Liberals tied rewards to work and enterprise while providing a safety net for need.

production-for-use.rationale: The tradition accepts production for profit under free enterprise, with government correcting abuses.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Truman treated business profits as compatible with rising wages and shared prosperity.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Liberals rejected communism and any dictatorship in favor of constitutional democracy.

collective-farming.rationale: Truman's farm program aimed to secure family farms, not collectivize them.

taxation-theft.rationale: Truman proposed raising billions in new taxes for public purposes; the founding objection was only to taxes imposed without consent.

harm-principle.rationale: Classical strands lean toward the harm principle while mid-century liberals accepted moral and social legislation, so the tradition is mixed.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The tradition grounds rights in individuals while later liberals accepted group-based remedies for discrimination, so it is mixed.

conscription.rationale: Truman asked Congress to adopt universal training, and Cold War liberals accepted the draft as part of containment.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The tradition places legitimacy in consent and participation through voting.

positive-liberty.rationale: Roosevelt's freedom from want made economic security part of liberty, which the sources identify as the core of American welfare-state liberalism.

organic-representation.rationale: American liberals represent citizens through elected legislatures and parties.

total-state.rationale: Kennedy explicitly rejected the super state while defending government action where it has a job to do.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on consent and law, not personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: The tradition embraced abolition of slavery and free labor.

universal-morality.rationale: The Declaration presents equality and unalienable rights as self-evident truths for all men.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Cold War liberals embraced Keynesian deficit spending in recessions, while still aiming at surpluses in booms.

economic-freedom.rationale: Classical liberal strands tie political to economic freedom, while New Deal liberals tied freedom to economic security, so they differ.

rule-by-example.rationale: The tradition relies on standing laws and constitutional government rather than rulers' virtue.

national-self-determination.rationale: Wilsonian and Rooseveltian internationalism backed self-determination of peoples and Truman welcomed free nations.

force-without-un.rationale: Liberals built the UN but also acted through NATO and in Vietnam without UN authorization; mixed.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Liberals trust reason but the tradition includes religious liberals; mixed.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The New Deal favored work relief, while later liberals expanded cash aid, so the strands differ.

class-collaboration.rationale: Truman described prosperity as a joint project of business, labor and government, and Cold War liberalism sought a labor-management balance.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Liberals backed women's suffrage and later women's equality; mid-century norms were more traditional, so low.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Northern liberals fought legal segregation, from Truman's civil rights program to the Civil Rights Act, against southern Democratic resistance.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Liberals saw the state as the instrument of the general welfare and of all citizens.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Truman urged developing oil and mineral resources rather than locking them up; later liberals reversed this.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The melting-pot ideal of the mid-century gave way to later pluralism; mixed.

elite-replacement.rationale: Liberals supported fair admission of immigrants and reject replacement conspiracy claims.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not a liberal priority in the American system.

national-mission.rationale: Cold War liberals held that the US should support free and democratic peoples everywhere; liberals divided after Vietnam.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Only later feminist liberals adopted this framing.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale infers the answer from the subject being or backing the establishment, not from a stated view of how politicians behave.

reviewHistory.rationale: Progressive liberals attacked corrupt machines, but the tradition defends its institutions; mixed lean against.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Some Progressive-era reformers backed eugenics, but the later tradition rejected it.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Truman's program of social security, health insurance, housing and school aid, and Kennedy's government that uses its full powers, go far beyond a minimal state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Declaration proclaims that all men are created equal, and equality before the law is a founding liberal principle.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Freedom of religion is a founding liberal principle.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Separation of church and state underlies liberal support for keeping religious instruction out of public schools.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Declaration states that governments derive their just powers from the consent of the governed, the foundation of American liberalism.

population-transfer.rationale: Expelling a minority seen as hostile contradicts the tradition's equal rights and due process, though liberals in Roosevelt's administration carried out Japanese American internment.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Liberals valued competition through antitrust but emphasized cooperation and security; mixed.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Some Cold War liberals backed curbs on communists while others opposed McCarthyism; split.

separated-powers.rationale: The tradition's constitutional framework divides power, and the Declaration condemned making judges dependent on the king's will.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Kennedy described liberals as caring about fighting poverty and Truman rejected trickle-down in favor of policies for the many.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Truman wanted Taft-Hartley repealed as unfair to workers, while accepting limits on jurisdictional strikes and secondary boycotts.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The tradition relies on elected representatives.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Cold War liberals sometimes accepted limits on liberty (Humphrey's detention proposal), but most opposed McCarthyism; low.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Truman asked for standby authority to set price ceilings on scarce essentials.

party-controls-media.rationale: Free speech and free press are among the founding liberal principles listed by the source.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Declaration condemned making the military independent of civil power; the military answers to civil government.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: American liberalism is a loose coalition without binding party discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Liberals backed the UN with a US veto, not supranational union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: In the US system the president commands the forces and picks the cabinet, which liberals accepted.

clerical-rule.rationale: Separation of church and state excludes clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Liberals backed the war effort and containment.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Roosevelt won four terms but the 22nd amendment later limited them; split.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Cold War liberals opposed isolationism and built the Western alliance system.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Truman pushed public low-rent housing, so rental housing is accepted.

people-in-arms.rationale: Truman backed standing forces plus universal training.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Jeffersonian strand idealized farmers while later liberals were urban; split.

death-penalty.rationale: Mid-century liberals did not consistently oppose capital punishment, while recent Democratic platforms call for abolition; split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The tradition is torn between free speech and decency norms.

minority-language-support.rationale: Bilingual education arrived only at the end of the tradition's peak, and earlier liberals favored English-language assimilation, so the strands differ.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberals tied economic progress to civil liberties and democracy.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Truman's program supported European recovery and aid to free peoples abroad.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The US had its own deterrent, which Cold War liberals maintained.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: New Deal liberals subordinated property to public purposes, while Lockean liberals treated it as a natural right; split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A dispute within Marxism that the liberal tradition never entered.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Mid-century liberals stressed resource development while later liberals adopted environmental caution, so the strands differ.

collective-defense.rationale: Cold War liberals built containment around the Western alliance and opposed isolationism.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Separation of church and state protects religion from the state as well.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.

reviewHistory.rationale: The American federal system gives states their own laws, but the tradition offers no view on autonomous regions joining a larger state.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Progressive taxation is a stated New Deal principle and Truman proposed higher rates for upper brackets.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Declaration indicts a king who refused assent to laws and acted outside them.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody rules were never part of the liberal program.

refugee-return.rationale: A question about other countries' conflicts that the tradition did not settle.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Freedom of religion, a founding liberal principle, includes the freedom to leave a faith.

women-must-cover.rationale: Contrary to religious freedom and individual liberty.

ban-cartels.rationale: Truman asked to strengthen antitrust laws, continuing Progressive-era trust-busting.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Liberals from Roosevelt to Truman worked to expand foreign trade through reciprocal agreements, opposing closed blocs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Mid-century liberals pursued plain tariff cuts while later liberals demanded labor standards in trade deals, so the strands differ.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The US was founded without monarchy or hereditary aristocracy.

history-own-civilization.rationale: School history curricula were not a liberal policy question at the tradition's peak.

patriotic-education.rationale: The tradition embraced civic patriotism but defended dissent, including objections to compulsory flag salutes, so it is mixed.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action arose late in the tradition; split.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Liberals believed that managed capitalism could overcome depressions.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Liberals backed fair employment rules barring discrimination by contractors and later the Civil Rights Act's limits on private discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Bill of Rights' guarantees of speech, press, religion and due process are named as the foundation of American liberalism.

elective-rulers.rationale: The tradition replaced hereditary monarchy with elected government resting on consent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Declaration justifies resisting and casting off a king who broke the laws and trust owed to the colonists.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The American tradition places the Constitution, not the legislature, above all, with powers separated.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Patrician liberals like Roosevelt embodied a sense of duty by the privileged, though the tradition framed help as public responsibility.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Kennedy's liberalism is an active faith in citizens shaping justice and freedom through public life.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Cold War liberals opposed communism as they had fascism, seeing both as hostile to freedom and democracy.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The founders condemned a military independent of civil power.

paid-care-work.rationale: Paying for domestic work was a demand of later feminists that the tradition's mainstream did not adopt or reject.

filial-duty.rationale: Family obligations between adults were not a political question for the tradition.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign takeovers were not a policy question at the tradition's peak.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Social Security is the tradition's signature pay-as-you-go program, which Truman sought to expand.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The founding grievance against taxes without consent places fiscal power in the legislature.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate impact doctrine came late in the tradition; mixed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Galbraithian liberals criticized affluence, but most celebrated mass prosperity; split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Cold War liberals were divided over covert action and support to insurgencies.

corporate-influence.rationale: Progressive and New Deal liberals saw concentrated business power as a threat to liberty and politics.

job-guarantee.rationale: New Deal work relief and the Full Employment bill pointed this way, but the tradition settled on fiscal policy rather than a guarantee; split.

non-intervention.rationale: Cold War liberals backed containment and foreign commitments, rejecting isolationism.

informal-organisation.rationale: The tradition works through parties, unions and organizations like the ADA.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Liberals built the UN but kept a US veto; mixed.

religious-nation.rationale: Freedom of religion and church-state separation define the nation in secular, civic terms.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on accepting or rejecting common ownership of production, or on private property in general, and the statement now asks only whether personal belongings should stay private where production is held in common.

reviewHistory.rationale: The tradition rejects common ownership of the means of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Cold War liberals pursued containment of communism, but opposed rollback and some later backed detente, so they stopped short of defeat.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Truman praised free enterprise for postwar gains when joined with good government.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Liberals saw the mixed economy as reformed capitalism, a vital center, but not a third system; ambiguous.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Mid-century law criminalized it widely and liberals did not prioritize repeal; later liberals opposed such laws; low.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Free speech, assembly and a free press are named foundations of liberalism.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Religious liberty rules out punishing blasphemy.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The tradition began as a revolt against rule for the benefit of a distant metropole.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Separation of church and state rejects religious tests for rulers.

participatory-democracy.rationale: A New Left demand the liberal mainstream did not share; mixed.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: A later framework beyond the tradition's peak.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Transgender rights arose long after the tradition's peak; only its most recent heirs took them up, so the tradition as a whole has no settled view.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not a question the tradition settled; liberal opinion on it is mixed.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Just powers come from the consent of the governed, though rights are said to come from the Creator.

social-market-economy.rationale: The New Deal and Fair Deal combined free enterprise with social insurance and fair competition rules rather than laissez-faire or state socialism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Truman insisted on armed forces to deter aggression.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Cold War liberals led the Western bloc and opposed isolationism.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The tradition was founded against hereditary rule and established a republic without monarchy or aristocracy.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The tradition built the Bretton Woods lenders but never took a position on their conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Liberals extended the vote to all adult citizens, including by the 15th and 19th amendments.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The tradition prized a free press and also worried about concentrated wealth, without settling on this claim.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The Declaration indicts arbitrary royal rule; the tradition demands government by known laws and independent judges.

racial-franchise.rationale: The tradition's civil rights strand fought for voting rights for all adult citizens.

online-participation.rationale: An internet-era question beyond the tradition's peak.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Progressive and New Deal liberals regarded concentrated economic power as a threat to liberty.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Church-state separation forbids state religion or irreligion alike.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The New Deal replaced reliance on private charity with federal relief and social insurance.

term-limits.rationale: Liberals backed Roosevelt's four terms while the 22nd Amendment limited later presidents, so the tradition is mixed.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: An internal church question the tradition left to churches.

rent-control.rationale: Truman asked Congress to extend and strengthen rent control.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The United States hosts no foreign bases, so the tradition never faced the question for itself.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Recognition of past genocides was not a settled question for the tradition.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Liberals taxed unearned income more heavily but accepted profits and dividends, so they lean neither way.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A question internal to recent feminist theory.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The tradition honors war dead civically, without religious martyrdom.

independent-unions.rationale: Liberals backed free, independent unions bargaining under the Wagner Act.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A question internal to socialism, which the tradition rejected.

online-anonymity.rationale: An internet-era question beyond the tradition's peak.

person-over-state.rationale: Kennedy rejected the super state and declared faith in individual citizens.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The tradition is secular in politics but includes religious liberals, so it takes no line.

gm-crops.rationale: A question beyond the tradition's peak.

free-public-college.rationale: The GI Bill and land-grant colleges expanded access, but free tuition was not a liberal demand at the peak.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its value rests on women's distinct roles, giving their values more weight, a claim about innate nature or no stated position, and the statement now asks only whether women tend to be more compassionate than men.

reviewHistory.rationale: A strand of later feminist thought the tradition did not settle.

arms-reduction.rationale: Cold War liberals pursued both a strong defense and arms control, so they lean neither way.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Wagner Act and Truman's call to restore it make collective bargaining central to the tradition.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Liberals promoted aid and trade for poor countries without accepting calls to rewrite world economic rules.

student-debt-relief.rationale: A recent question beyond the tradition's peak.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not a framework the tradition used, though New Deal programs targeted the poor South.

farm-price-support.rationale: Truman called for price supports to secure parity income for farmers, building on the New Deal's Agricultural Adjustment Act.

workers-own-party.rationale: Liberals saw labor as part of the Democratic coalition, not a separate party.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Truman opposed Taft-Hartley, which had permitted state right-to-work laws.

premarital-sex.rationale: A cultural question the tradition's politics did not settle.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Some liberals backed income guarantees around 1970 while others defended social insurance, so the tradition is mixed.

women-suffrage.rationale: The source credits the liberal tradition with the 19th amendment's extension of the franchise to women.

national-church-status.rationale: Church-state separation rules out an established church.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The tradition demands due process and trial by jury.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Truman wanted social security extended to all workers rather than limited to the poorest.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Liberals admired civil disobedience against segregation yet stressed lawful change, so the tradition is mixed.

police-more-powers.rationale: Cold War liberals backed high military spending and strong defense, but the tradition is wary of police power over civil liberties, so it is mixed overall. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Social Security and unemployment insurance are the tradition's signature achievements, and Truman sought to widen coverage and raise benefits rather than cut them. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

notes: The tradition spans strands that disagree: the founding and Jeffersonian classical strand trusted markets and property rights, while New Deal liberals subordinated them to economic security, so those statements are 0. Cold War liberals divided over Vietnam (hawks such as Henry Jackson, doves such as George McGovern) and over curbs on communists. Positions on abortion, LGBT rights, climate and gender came only after the tradition's peak and are low-confidence readings of how its heirs developed.
